#!/bin/sh
set -eu

ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$ROOT"
HOOK_ROOT="$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
GIT_LOCAL_ENV_VARS="$(git rev-parse --local-env-vars)"

run_without_git_local_env() (
  # Git exports repository-local variables while running hooks.  Several script
  # tests create temporary repositories; keep those tests independent of this
  # checkout.
  unset $GIT_LOCAL_ENV_VARS
  "$@"
)

# A merge commit can be syntactically valid while its index has been reset to
# the first-parent tree.  That failure mode silently discarded clean incoming
# additions on issue-109 and issue-110 (issue #222).  Check the pending index
# before every other gate, including the documented blanket hook bypass: a
# missing incoming path is valid only when the branch deleted a base path.
MERGE_HEAD_PATH="$(git rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD)"
if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking the merge result for silent incoming loss."
  python3 "$HOOK_ROOT/local/bin/merge_loss_guard.py" --repo "$ROOT"
fi

# Scope-control guard (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-01, the issue-0007 overbuild):
# workflow scaffolding is budgeted at <=1000 changed lines per commit (400 until the owner raised it on 2026-09-05).  This is
# mechanical enforcement — repeated verbal correction of scaffolding bloat did
# not stick, so the budget lives in the hook.  The override env var is granted
# by the OWNER per commit, never self-granted by an agent session.  Runs
# before the ACMR early-exit so deletion-only commits are counted too
# (numstat includes deletions; PR 7 round 3, F8), and before the
# MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS exit so a blanket hook skip cannot launder the
# owner-only budget override.
# A merge that carries main stages already-reviewed content.  A merge head
# contained in github/main measures the budget against MERGE_HEAD; a merge head
# that contains github/main (a parent branch of a stack that already merged
# main; owner decision 2026-09-05) measures it against github/main, so inherited
# main content counts zero while the PR's cumulative workflow diff and any
# side-branch content beyond main still count.  Any other side-branch merge
# stays budgeted against HEAD.
if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ] &&
    git merge-base --is-ancestor MERGE_HEAD refs/remotes/github/main 2>/dev/null; then
  BUDGET_BASE="$(git rev-parse MERGE_HEAD)"
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: main-history merge; budget measured against MERGE_HEAD."
elif [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ] &&
    git merge-base --is-ancestor refs/remotes/github/main MERGE_HEAD 2>/dev/null; then
  BUDGET_BASE="$(git rev-parse refs/remotes/github/main)"
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: non-main merge carrying github/main; workflow-layer content beyond github/main is budgeted."
else
  BUDGET_BASE=""
  if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ]; then
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: non-main merge; workflow-layer merge content is budgeted."
  fi
fi
INFRA_CHANGED="$(git diff --cached --numstat $BUDGET_BASE -- local/ .githooks/ \
  scripts/tests/test_dispatch.py scripts/tests/test_github_workflow.py \
  scripts/tests/test_lake_root.py scripts/tests/test_pre_push_hook.py \
  scripts/tests/test_ready_packets.py scripts/tests/test_merge_loss_guard.py \
  | awk '{added=$1; deleted=$2; if (added != "-") total+=added+deleted} END {print total+0}')"
if [ "${INFRA_CHANGED:-0}" -gt 1000 ] && [ "${MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE:-}" != "1" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: staged workflow-layer change is ${INFRA_CHANGED} lines (budget: 1000)."
  echo "Scope control (local/personas/main.md): the budget is PER EPISODE, not per"
  echo "commit — serial oversized commits are the same violation and show in the"
  echo "telemetry. Shrink the change, or ask the OWNER to authorize this commit"
  echo "with MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE=1 (self-granting it is a protocol breach)."
  exit 1
fi

if [ "${MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS:-}" = "1" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit hook skipped by MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1."
  exit 0
fi

STAGED_FILES="$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR)"
if [ -z "$STAGED_FILES" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking staged whitespace."
# Paper mirrors under references/ are byte-faithful captures of external
# arXiv sources (see references/*/README.md); their inherited trailing
# whitespace is part of the fidelity claim and must not be "fixed", so they
# are exempt from the whitespace gate (local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md,
# 2026-08-30).
git diff --cached --check -- ':(exclude)references/'

if printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_FILES" | grep -Eq '^scripts/(.*\.py|tests/.*)$'; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: running scripts/tests unit tests."
  run_without_git_local_env python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'
fi

if printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_FILES" | grep -Eq \
  '^(blueprint/src/.*\.(tex|sty|cls)|scripts/(check_blueprint_latex|tex_utils)\.py|scripts/tests/test_check_blueprint_latex\.py|\.githooks/pre-commit)$'; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking blueprint LaTeX conventions."
  python3 scripts/check_blueprint_latex.py --root blueprint/src
fi

if ! printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_FILES" | grep -Eq \
  '^(MIPStarRE/|MIPStarRE\.lean|blueprint/src/|blueprint/lean_decls|scripts/(audit_new_proof_obligation_metadata|audit_paper_facing_proof_debt|audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses|audit_unfaithful_markers|audit_lean_axiom_declarations|check_blueprint_latex|check_paper_gap_note_style|check_statement_paper_origin|check_source_statement_changes|blueprint_lean_sync|lean_header_utils|tex_utils)\.py|docs/(CONTRIBUTING|project_conventions|anti_patterns|blueprint_style_guide|formalization-patterns|proof_frontier_review)\.md|docs/paper-gaps/|\.github/(actions|prompts|workflows)/|AGENTS\.md)'; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: no statement-integrity files staged."
  exit 0
fi

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking changed paper-gap note structure."
python3 scripts/check_paper_gap_note_style.py --root . --staged --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking statement-like paper-origin citations."
python3 scripts/check_statement_paper_origin.py --root .

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking new proof-obligation metadata."
python3 scripts/audit_new_proof_obligation_metadata.py --root . --staged --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking paper-facing proof-debt headers."
echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: do not close proof gaps by adding non-paper bridge/package hypotheses."
python3 scripts/audit_paper_facing_proof_debt.py --root . --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking conclusion-shaped hypotheses."
python3 scripts/audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses.py --root . --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking unfaithful-dependency markers."
python3 scripts/audit_unfaithful_markers.py --root . --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking explicit LDT axiom declarations."
python3 scripts/audit_lean_axiom_declarations.py --root . --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: ok."
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

if [ "${MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS:-}" = "1" ]; then
  # checked-push sets an expected tuple when only the expensive gate is skipped.
  if [ -n "${MIPSTARRE_EXPECTED_PUSH_TUPLE:-}" ]; then
    if ! IFS= read -r ACTUAL_PUSH_TUPLE; then
      echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: checked ref is already current."
      exit 0
    fi
    if IFS= read -r EXTRA_PUSH_TUPLE; then
      echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: expected exactly one advertised ref tuple." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$ACTUAL_PUSH_TUPLE" != "$MIPSTARRE_EXPECTED_PUSH_TUPLE" ]; then
      echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: advertised ref tuple changed after preflight." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: confirmed preflight ref tuple."
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push hook skipped by MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1."
  exit 0
fi

ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$ROOT"

CHANGED_FILE_LIST="$(mktemp)"
CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST" "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST"' EXIT
BLUEPRINT_WEB_SMOKE_RAN=0

ZERO_SHA="0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"

run_outside_git_env() (
  for name in $(git rev-parse --local-env-vars); do
    unset "$name"
  done
  "$@"
)

lean_file_to_module() {
  path="${1%.lean}"
  printf '%s\n' "$path" | tr '/' '.'
}

while read LOCAL_REF LOCAL_SHA REMOTE_REF REMOTE_SHA
do
  if [ -z "${LOCAL_SHA:-}" ] || [ "$LOCAL_SHA" = "$ZERO_SHA" ]; then
    continue
  fi

  if [ "$REMOTE_SHA" = "$ZERO_SHA" ]; then
    if git rev-parse --verify origin/main >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      BASE_SHA="$(git merge-base "$LOCAL_SHA" origin/main)"
    else
      BASE_SHA="$(git rev-list --max-parents=0 "$LOCAL_SHA" | tail -n 1)"
    fi
  else
    BASE_SHA="$REMOTE_SHA"
  fi

  git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR "$BASE_SHA" "$LOCAL_SHA" -- >> "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST"
done

sort -u "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST" -o "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST"
grep -E '^(MIPStarRE/.*\.lean|MIPStarRE\.lean)$' "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST" \
  > "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST" || true

if [ ! -s "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: no changed tracked files detected."
  exit 0
fi

if [ -s "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST" ]; then

if [ -s "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST" ] ||
    grep -Eq '^scripts/(check_oversized_lean_files\.py|tests/test_check_oversized_lean_files\.py)$' \
      "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST"; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: checking Lean file length guard."
  run_outside_git_env python3 scripts/check_oversized_lean_files.py --root .
fi

if grep -Eq '^(MIPStarRE/LDT/.*\.lean|MIPStarRE/LDT\.lean|MIPStarRE\.lean)$' "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST"; then

  else
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: checking LDT axiom audit."
    run_outside_git_env lake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean
  fi
fi

if grep -Eq '^(MIPStarRE/|MIPStarRE\.lean$|blueprint/src/|blueprint/lean_decls|scripts/(audit_new_proof_obligation_metadata|audit_paper_facing_proof_debt|audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses|audit_unfaithful_markers|audit_lean_axiom_declarations|check_paper_gap_note_style|check_statement_paper_origin|check_source_statement_changes|blueprint_lean_sync|lean_header_utils)\.py|docs/(CONTRIBUTING|project_conventions|anti_patterns|blueprint_style_guide|formalization-patterns|proof_frontier_review)\.md|docs/paper-gaps/|\.github/(actions|prompts|workflows)/|AGENTS\.md)' "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST"; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: checking statement-integrity audits."

1:# Incident and observation log
2:Dated bullets, one incident each: symptom → diagnosis → fix → lesson.
3:This file is the raw feed for `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.
4:## 2026-09-05
5:- **Owner-side `.lake` relocation shim.** Worktree build directories consumed the
6:  87%-full root volume, whose fsync writes measured nine times slower than the
7:  NVMe ZFS pool. Temporary owner launchers moved each `.lake` to `/data` before
8:  bootstrap, but merge cleanup left the external directory behind. Issue #190
9:  replaces that untracked ordering dependency with an opt-in Lake root shared by
10:  setup and warming, plus guarded post-worktree cleanup. Lesson: storage
11:  placement and lifecycle cleanup belong in the workflow boundary that creates
12:  and retires the worktree.
13:- **External Lake-root review guards.** PR #198 round-1 review found that root
14:  aliases, symlinked branch ancestors, `hot-main` targets, and the Codex sandbox
15:  were outside the initial safety model. The repair canonicalizes before create
16:  and delete, preserves both containment boundaries, and grants only the checked
17:  branch target to writable sessions. Lesson: external placement needs filesystem
18:  and execution-sandbox containment to be designed as one boundary.
19:- **Canonical Lake target ownership.** PR #198 reviews found shared-cache and
20:  checkout overlap, nested or aliased branch targets, detached owners, and silent
21:  retry cleanup. Setup and cleanup now accept one-component branches, protect
22:  packages, `hot-main`, and every checkout, and compare canonical ownership;
23:  retries warn when the root is unavailable. Lesson: destructive cleanup needs
24:  collision-free names and operator-visible ownership inputs at deletion time.
25:## 2026-08-30
26:- **Stale seed clone.** Symptom: files copied from the sibling `../MIPStarRE`
27:  checkout were dated Jul 5 while upstream main was Aug 25. Diagnosis: the
28:  local clone's fetched refs were two months old; `git status` against a stale
29:  `origin/main` looked clean. Fix: `git fetch`, then `git archive origin/main`
30:  overlay plus replay of upstream deletions. Lesson: verify snapshot freshness
31:  against the remote SHA (`gh api .../branches/main`) before seeding, not
32:  against local tracking refs.
33:- **Warm-cache invalidation by toolchain bump.** The upstream snapshot moved
34:  to Lean v4.32.0 while the copied `.lake` was built on v4.31.0; the planned
35:  zero-cost cache seed became a full rebuild (25,052 s, see `builds.jsonl`).
36:  Lesson: the hot-cache keyhash (lean-toolchain + lake-manifest.json +
37:  lakefile.toml) is the first thing to check when estimating seed cost.
38:- **Dirty vendored package blocks `lake exe cache get`.** Symptom: cache
39:  fetch aborted with "Your local changes ... would be overwritten by
40:  checkout" for `.lake/packages/proofwidgets/widget/js/lake.trace`.
41:  Diagnosis: past builds mutate files inside the vendored package's git tree;
42:  a CoW-copied `.lake` carries that dirt. Fix: `git reset --hard` inside the
43:  package. Lesson: worktree bootstrap must reset vendored package trees
44:  before cache fetch (ported into `worktree-setup.sh`).
45:- **Mathlib cache partial miss.** 20 of ~9k cache files failed to download;
46:  `lake build` compiled those modules locally. No action needed; noted as a
47:  normal degraded mode of `lake exe cache get`.
48:- **Workflow critic stalled on oversized prompt.** Symptom: the study
49:  workflow's final critic agent made no progress for 6×180 s and the run
50:  failed after its 7 readers had finished. Diagnosis: the critic prompt
51:  embedded the full 180 KB merged JSON of all reader results. Fix: harvested
52:  reader results from the journal; the main session performed the critique
53:  itself over a rendered digest. Lesson: pass large fan-in data to agents by
54:  file path, not inline; cap inline context in synthesis prompts.
55:- **Verification pass caught four live defects in the drafted layer.** The
56:  7-builder Opus draft passed syntax/smoke on the data layer, but the Fable
57:  verifier live-demonstrated: (1) the merge gate could never accept a reviewed
58:  PR (verdict-file glob mismatch); (2) the cap-time forced review was a
59:  guaranteed no-op (review refused under the fix lock its own caller held);
60:  (3) three uncoordinated machine-wide build locks; (4) `printf '%04d'` octal
61:  crash on ids 0008/0009. All fixed same day (`EVOLUTION.md` entry); post-fix
62:  smoke rerun: issue → PR → green CI fixture → review verdict → merge gate
63:  PASS → full no-ff merge with bookkeeping. Lesson: multi-agent drafts need an
64:  adversarial cross-cutting verifier; per-builder self-tests missed every
65:  cross-script contract break.

103:  authoritative for merge bookkeeping, and the reviewer reads them.

108:  added to `local/README.md` — always invoke workflow tools via the primary
109:  checkout's path. Lesson: a protocol fix in versioned tooling is not
110:  deployed until every live branch carries it; invocation discipline (or a
111:  merge into open branches) bridges the gap.
112:- **Review-fix loop reached the faithfulness layer (stage 3).** Rounds:
113:  33 → 26 → 18 findings. Round 1 was mostly writer errors; round 2 mostly
114:  boundary domains plus register violations introduced by round-1 fixers;
115:  round 3 exposed two genuine source obstructions (the classical-test
116:  instantiation at dimension 2m+2 vs the m | q admissibility, and
117:  supremum attainment in the symmetrization lemma), which per the

123:  reviewer audited proof sketches of imported theorems at formalization
124:  depth, invented obligations for heuristic repair sketches in gap notes,
125:  and relitigated a policy sanctioned in a ledger it cannot see from the

/-!
# The directly indexed low-degree game

The low-degree game used by the Pauli-basis combining argument is needed in
dimension `2 * m + 2`.  The existing conditionally linear game represents a
coordinate index by an equally sized fiber in the scalar field and therefore
requires the dimension to divide the field size.  This file gives the separate
directly indexed variant which samples that index directly.

The geometric line carrier records the sampled coordinate, and line evaluation
uses an `Option` outcome rather than assigning a value when a point does not
determine one.  The game retains the point, axis-line, and diagonal-line answer
formats and the nine ordered type branches of the original low-degree game.

The `Transport` modules relate the direct game to the seed-indexed game and to
the low individual degree test: `Transport.Correspondence`
identifies coordinates, answers, and the question law of the two QPBT
presentations; `Transport.SeedFiber` dilates a seed-indexed strategy to a
direct strategy by a correlated residue register, and `Transport.SeedFiberValue`
shows that the dilation preserves the value exactly; `Transport.Questions`
reads LDT lines as canonical direct questions and rebases direct answers;
`Transport.Strategy` reads one coordinate of a projective direct strategy as
an LDT projective strategy, with exact Born-weight formulas for both
constructions; `Transport.Consistency` reexpresses the three
single-polynomial LDT consistency relations in direct coordinates, the first
two at a fixed tuple coordinate; and
`Transport.BranchComparison`, `Transport.DiagonalRecursion`, and
`Transport.PassConversion` convert a value bound of the direct game into the
pass hypothesis of the low individual degree theorem for every
coordinate strategy.  `GameValue` supplies the rejection calculus relating the
direct value to the LDT branch weights.  `Transport.Error` carries the
scalar half of the transport: the auxiliary sampling parameter with which
the low individual degree theorem is applied, bounds on the three terms of its
error function, and the absorption of the resulting simultaneous-measurement
estimate into the error function of `lem:ld-soundness`; and
`Transport.Simultaneous` applies that theorem to every coordinate, carries
the Schwartz--Zippel collision estimate to the direct polynomial
representatives, and proves the polynomial-tuple conclusion of
`lem:ld-soundness` for simultaneity parameter `1`.  It also records why the
coordinate conclusions do not determine simultaneous measurements for larger
parameters.  `Transport.PointAgreement` reads the point-agreement branch of
either game as a consistency estimate, and `SeedIndexedSoundness` transports
the polynomial-tuple conclusions back to the seed-indexed game `ldGame` by
compressing the correlated residue register, recovering the global polynomial
relation from the two point relations and the point-agreement branch.

For a general simultaneity parameter, the reduction introduces the combined
parameters `DirectLdParams.combined`, of dimension `m + k` and simultaneity
parameter `1`; the combining map on polynomial tuples and its individual-degree
bound; the substitution recovering the components of a combined polynomial,
which exhibits the combining map as injective; and the Schwartz--Zippel
collision estimate for two linear forms in the combining variables; and the
combined strategy itself, which answers every question of the combined game by
measuring one question of the original strategy and relabelling its outcome,
together with its projectivity, the identification of the measured questions on
each sample of the combined game, and the transport of its value.  The recovery
of the components of a combined outcome costs `(m + k) d / q` in the two point
relations.  The general-simultaneity theorem combines these constructions, and
the scalar estimate absorbs the resulting error into the error function of
`lem:ld-soundness`; see
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, the subsection on the combining
reduction.

## References

The underlying game is `def:ld-game` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with source origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
The need for the directly indexed repair in Chapter 15 is explained around
`rem:qld-4-7-divisibility` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1257-1293` and in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
-/

import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Observables.WinImplications.Consistency

/-!
# Winning implications for strategy observables

This module states the seven consequences of success in the Pauli basis test
and their operator-distance companions. It also constructs the actual Magic
Square strategy associated with a Pauli tuple and records the two observable
consequences used by the expanded-state argument.

The root names retain the blueprint-facing API; their proofs are in the
corresponding `WinImplications` leaves, re-exported here for compatibility.

## References

The declarations formalize `lem:qld-win-implications` and
`lem:qld-win-implications-obs` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:505-733`. Their paper source
is `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:192-354`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
open MIPStarRE.Quantum

noncomputable section

/-- The consistency subtest bounds the off-diagonal defect of the two strategy
measurement families. This is item 1 of `lem:qld-win-implications`, paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:197-199`, blueprint
`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:515-522`. -/
theorem win_cons :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε),
      0 ≤ ε →
      consistencyDefect (pauliQuestionMarginal P)
        (fun question a => heteroKron
          ((S.strategyMeasurement .alice question).effect a) 1)
        (fun question a => heteroKron 1
          ((S.strategyMeasurement .bob question).effect a))
        S.toStrategy.ψ ≤ C * ε := WinImplications.win_cons

/-- The low-degree subtest bounds completed line-evaluation classes against
completed point measurements. This is item 2 of
`lem:qld-win-implications`, paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:200-204`, blueprint
`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:523-548`. -/
theorem win_low_degree :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε),
      0 ≤ ε → ∀ W : PauliKind,
      consistencyDefect (linePointDist P.toLdParams)
        (fun sample a => heteroKron
          ((S.lineEvalMeas .alice W sample.1 sample.2).effect a) 1)
        (fun sample a => heteroKron 1
          ((S.pointMeasOption .bob W sample.2).effect a))
        S.toStrategy.ψ ≤ C * ε := WinImplications.win_low_degree

/-- The Pauli-basis consistency subtest compares point values with evaluated
low-degree encodings of Pauli answers. This is item 3 of
`lem:qld-win-implications`, paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:205-209`, blueprint
`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:549-566`. -/
theorem win_pauli_basis_cons :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε),
      0 ≤ ε → ∀ W : PauliKind,
      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
        (fun u a => heteroKron ((S.pointMeas .alice W u).effect a) 1)
        (fun u a => heteroKron 1 ((S.pauliEvalMeas .bob W u).effect a))
        S.toStrategy.ψ ≤ C * ε := WinImplications.win_pauli_basis_cons

/-- On commuting tuples, Pair/W answers agree with the corresponding
component of Pair answers. This is item 4 of `lem:qld-win-implications`, paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:210-231`, blueprint
`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:567-582`. -/
theorem win_comm :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε),
      0 ≤ ε → ∀ W : PauliKind,
      consistencyDefect (commTupleDist P)
        (fun ω a => heteroKron
          ((S.pairWMeas .alice W ω.1 ω.2.1 ω.2.2.1 ω.2.2.2).effect a) 1)
        (fun ω a => heteroKron 1 ((S.pairComponentMeas .bob W ω).effect a))
        S.toStrategy.ψ ≤ C * ε := WinImplications.win_comm

/-- On commuting tuples, trace-coarse-grained point answers agree with Pair/W
